title: Gold Price Crash: What It Means for MCX Gold and Gold Mini Put Sellers
summary: See why gold fell in November 2026, how a hedge changed one MCX Gold Mini put seller’s loss, and what happens to in-the-money puts on 27 November.
body_markdown:
On Friday, 20 November, MCX December Gold futures closed at ₹1,21,949 per 10 grams, down 4.32% on the day. For a trader who had sold the ₹1,25,000 Gold Mini put, the more important number was ₹3,960. That was the last quoted premium on a put that had been valued at ₹1,097.50 the previous day. **Across one Gold Mini lot, that change worked out to a ₹28,625 loss before costs.**


A trader who had also bought the ₹1,20,000 put for the same expiry saw a smaller loss of ₹15,635 on the two legs together. Here’s how those figures work and why Friday, 27 November matters for anyone still holding an MCX gold option.


## Why did gold prices fall in November 2026?


By Friday afternoon in New York, global spot gold was trading at $3,514.08 per troy ounce, down about 9.4% for the week. Traders were pricing in a possible US Federal Reserve rate increase in December. Gold pays no interest, so higher expected rates make interest-bearing dollar assets more attractive.


A stronger US dollar also weighed on bullion. Reuters reported that some investors were selling gold to cover losses on equity positions, adding to the pressure.


In India, December Gold Mini futures closed Friday at ₹1,21,871 per 10 grams, down from ₹1,27,499 on Thursday. That move took Gold Mini below the ₹1,25,000 put strike with a week still to go before option expiry. For the seller, the decline in futures and the time left on the option both mattered.

## How much did one MCX Gold Mini put lose on Friday?


Gold Mini options are quoted in rupees per 10 grams. One GOLDM lot covers 100 grams, so **every ₹1 change in the quoted option premium is worth ₹10 per lot** . Standard GOLD covers 1 kg, making the same ₹1 premium change worth ₹100 per lot. The two contracts have their own traded premiums. See the[MCX Gold and Gold Mini lot sizes](https://algotest.in/blog/gold-lot-size/) .


The table uses the 20 November GOLDM option-chain snapshot for the **27 November 2026 expiry** . The previous values are calculated from the daily changes shown in the chain.

The short put became ₹2,862.50 more expensive per 10 grams. Multiplying by 10 gives the one-lot loss of ₹28,625. The lower-strike put gained ₹12,990, offsetting about 45% of that loss. Buying the hedge had cost ₹3,160 for the lot and reduced the initial premium collected from ₹10,975 to ₹7,815.


These figures measure the change between two sets of quotes. A trader closing both legs would receive the available bid on the long put and pay the available ask on the short put. Different fill prices, brokerage and other charges would change the realised result.


## Why was the Gold Mini put worth more than its intrinsic value?


A put gives its buyer the right to sell the underlying futures at the strike. At Friday’s Gold Mini futures close of ₹1,21,871, the ₹1,25,000 put was already **₹3,129 in the money** . Its quoted premium was ₹3,960. The remaining ₹831 per 10 grams was time value. The trader buying it still had a week in which gold could fall further.


That distinction matters even more for the hedge. The ₹1,20,000 put was still out of the money on Friday, yet it gained ₹1,299 per 10 grams over the day. A lower-strike hedge can therefore offset part of a sell-off **before** gold reaches the hedge strike.


## What would the same position lose at expiry?


Suppose December Gold Mini futures finish at **₹1,22,000 at option expiry** . This is an illustrative price for 27 November. Using the same assumed entry premiums as above:


-


**Short ₹1,25,000 put alone.** The put finishes ₹3,000 in the money. Subtract the ₹1,097.50 premium received and multiply by 10. The option loss is **₹19,025 per Gold Mini lot** , before costs.


-


**Short put plus the ₹1,20,000 hedge.** At this settlement price, the lower put expires worthless. The trader collected ₹781.50 net per 10 grams, so the combined option loss is **₹22,185** . At this particular price, the hedge cost makes the spread’s expiry result worse by ₹3,160.


-


**If futures finish at or below ₹1,20,000.** The two strikes are ₹5,000 apart. After deducting the net credit, the spread’s maximum expiry loss is **₹42,185 per Gold Mini lot** . The unhedged short put continues losing ₹10 per lot for each additional ₹1 decline in the futures settlement price.


The lower put helped on 20 November because it still had time value. At expiry, its protection depends on where gold settles. These payoffs cover the options through expiry. Any futures position carried afterwards has its own P&L.


AlgoTest’s Gold Mini option chain at 11:30 PM IST on 20 November 2026. For the 27 November expiry, the ₹1,25,000 put traded at ₹4,116.50 and the ₹1,20,000 put at ₹1,719.50 per 10 grams.


## What happens to an in-the-money MCX gold put on 27 November?


Both Gold and Gold Mini options expire on Friday, 27 November 2026. An assigned short put becomes a long position in the underlying December futures at the strike price. The position then requires futures margin and gains or loses as the futures price moves. The 23 November bullion option expiry applies to Silver Mini. See the[MCX expiry calendar](https://algotest.in/blog/mcx-expiry-dates/) .


Consider the ₹1,22,000 settlement example again. The ₹1,25,000 short put is in the money and the ₹1,20,000 long put expires worthless. A trader who carried the spread through assignment could therefore be left **long one Gold Mini futures lot** . The hedge’s expiry loss limit ends with the options.


The underlying Gold and Gold Mini futures expire on **4 December 2026** and are subject to staggered delivery. Broker deadlines can come earlier. For example, Zerodha’s November bulletin asks clients to maintain adequate futures margin before **7 PM IST on 27 November** to avoid a square-off. Its separate delivery bulletin asks clients to close the December bullion futures before **10:30 PM IST on 1 December** to avoid a broker square-off ahead of delivery. Check the deadlines your own broker applies.

## FAQs


### Why did gold prices fall in November 2026?


A stronger US dollar and expectations of a December US Federal Reserve rate hike weighed on gold. Some investors also sold gold to cover stock-market losses. By the afternoon of 20 November in New York, global spot gold was down about 9.4% for the week.


### How much did a seller of the MCX Gold Mini ₹1,25,000 put lose on 20 November?


The one-day loss was **₹28,625 per lot** at quoted prices, before costs. The put premium rose from ₹1,097.50 to ₹3,960 per 10 grams, making it more expensive to buy back. One Gold Mini lot covers 100 grams, so the ₹2,862.50 premium increase is multiplied by 10.


### Can a lower-strike put protect a Gold Mini seller before gold reaches that strike?


Yes. On 20 November, Gold Mini futures closed at ₹1,21,871, still above the ₹1,20,000 strike. With a week left to expiry, that put’s premium rose from ₹316 to ₹1,615 per 10 grams. Owning one lot offset **₹12,990** of the short put’s loss, reducing the combined one-day loss to **₹15,635** at quoted prices, before costs.


### What is the maximum loss on the ₹1,25,000–₹1,20,000 Gold Mini put spread?


At the example’s entry premiums, the maximum loss **at option expiry is ₹42,185 per lot** , before costs. The strikes are ₹5,000 apart and the seller collected a net premium of ₹781.50 per 10 grams. If Gold Mini futures settle at or below ₹1,20,000, the calculation is (₹5,000 − ₹781.50) × 10.


### What happens if an MCX Gold Mini put expires in the money on 27 November 2026?


If the short put is assigned, the seller takes a long position in December Gold Mini futures at the put strike. The seller then needs futures margin, and subsequent price moves create fresh gains or losses. For this expiry, Zerodha asks clients to maintain sufficient margin before 7 PM IST on 27 November to avoid square-off.
